excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content:
<@427491045308235776>, I summarized here the benchmark against that branch for `go-ipa` and `go-verkle`: https://hackmd.io/@jsign/Syq7DcWIs
The TL;DR is that there're regressions. Most of the regressions seem to be related to allocs (and thus some CPU impact).
The only way to potentially solve this is to look case by case why and see if:
- That relates to some optimization we did before that isn't in the original gnark-crypto
- Maybe new extra allocs in the updated version implementations.

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content: So I'd guess the ideal thing would be to figure out each case, see if we can save the same allocations as we did before, and try to upstream as much as possible to gnark-crypto. (And eventually see if any impl changed in a way that we can't make it "on par" with what we have today).
